question.text: In the AIF context, "vintage year" refers to:

answer.text: The age of the fund manager
The milestone year in which the first influx of investment capital is delivered, with the fund in its initial investment mode
The year in which the oldest portfolio company was incorporated
A reference to wine-industry investments held by the fund

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines vintage year as the milestone year in which the first influx of investment capital is delivered. In the AIF context, vintage years are the years during which the fund is in its initial investment mode. Boom or bottom-cycle vintage years can affect entry valuations and ultimate returns. The Trap: Option B reflects the source definition. The other options reframe vintage year as either a personal attribute of the manager, the age of an investee, or an unrelated industry reference. Note: The earlier wording centred on comparing funds launched in the same year for peer benchmarking. That formulation was broader than the checked workbook, which only supports the milestone-year definition and the market-cycle impact, so the stem and explanation are now tied directly to the source.
